```suggestion
				Returns [code]true[/code] if the current animation is valid but not currently playing.
```
Following the above comment's suggestion, it becomes like this.

However, having `is_paused()` but not `is_stopped()` might be unbalanced.

So, as suggested above, it might be better to only expose `is_valid()` and simply provide sample code like the following to explain the distinction between `stop` and `pause` on the class documents. But `is_valid()` is bit ambiguous and may conflict with other core concepts in the future, so bind it as `is_current_valid()` might be preferable.

```gdscript
# Paused.
!player.is_playing() && player.is_current_valid()

# Stopped.
!player.is_playing() && !player.is_current_valid()
```

> The fundamental issue should be that playback.current.from isn't exposed to GDScript

But isn't this just what [`current_animation_position`](https://docs.godotengine.org/en/stable/classes/class_animationplayer.html#class-animationplayer-property-current-animation-position) is?

> you might consider simply exposing AnimationPlayer::is_valid()

This isn't really a problem. Wouldn't this work the same?
```gdscript
func is_valid():
	return current_animation_position
```
The problem arises if the animation is paused right when the animation starts (which maybe doesn't really matter), and would also imply the animation is paused if the animation is at the last frame.

There's also a workaround mentioned in the [proposal](https://github.com/godotengine/godot-proposals/issues/13208), but I think this PR aims to make the process easier/more straightforward, because you technically can know if an animation is playing using `is_processing()`

I *do* believe that there might be a better implementation not needing a flag that is unused by the core engine, but I think the intention was to know if the animation was paused by `AnimationPlayer.pause()`.

I do agree, and I did consider adding an `is_stopped()` method but that didn't sit right with me.

Maybe in practice this is the right approach, but this renders this PR useless because one can also do:
```gdscript
# Paused.
!player.is_playing() && player.current_animation_position

# Stopped.
!player.is_playing() && !player.current_animation_position
```

The check for playback.current.from in current_animation_position was recently added, but regardless, it returns an error and a float value. It is not a function that directly checks for the existence of playback.current.from, so your point is incorrect.

Simply having an existence check for playback.current.from, combined with is_playing as described below, allows the state to be verified. This resolves the issue pointed out in the proposal.

body:
As explained above, `current_animation_position` currently returns an error if `!playback.current.from`, so that is not the correct approach. What is needed is a function that only checks for the existence of `playback.current.from`.

Then this PR should be: "Expose `is_current_valid()` to check existence `playback.current.from` for determining pause and stop".

BTW, there is a confusion that GDScript's `get_current_animation` currently looks at `playback.assigned` internally.

What should be exposed here is `playback.current`. While I'm not sure what to call it in GDScript, we should at least avoid the term `current_animation`. Therefore, I think terms like `current` or `current_state` would be preferable.

Sorry, I have mistook `playback.current.from` for a variable storing the current position in the animation 😅.

Yes I did expose is_valid and the behavior seems to work flawlessly. I'll Update the PR accordingly.

Sorry. I mistook `playback.current.from` for the current position in the animation. 😅. I went on on test exposing `is_valid()`, and it worked flawlessly! I will go on about updating the PR accordingly.

I prefer `is_animation_active()` tho 👀

This is what I settled on.
```
Returns [code]true[/code] if the an animation is currently active. An animation is active if it was played by calling [method play] and was not finished yet, or was stopped by calling [method stop].
This can be used to check whether an animation is currently paused or stopped.
[codeblock]
var is_paused = not is_playing() and is_animation_active()
var is_stopped = not is_playing() and not is_animation_active()
[/codeblock]
```
